events.title: Penda of Mercia defeats and kills Oswald of Northumbria at Maserfield
events.description: Penda of Mercia, allied with the Welsh kingdom of Gwynedd, defeated King Oswald of Northumbria, probably at Oswestry in Shropshire. Oswald was killed and later venerated as a saint, and the victory made Penda the most powerful ruler in England.

events.title: Mercia and Wessex defeat a Viking army at Tettenhall
events.description: The allied forces of Mercia and Wessex under Edward the Elder and Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians, defeated Northumbrian Vikings near Tettenhall, according to the chronicler Æthelweard. It was the last major Danish army to raid England for nearly a century.

events.title: Caliph al-Muti' abdicates and his son al-Ta'i succeeds him
events.description: After the Turkic commander Sabuktakin seized Baghdad from the Buyid Izz al-Dawla, the aged and paralysed caliph al-Muti' was induced to abdicate. His son became caliph as al-Ta'i, the first father-to-son succession of the caliphate since 902.

events.title: Henry I is crowned King of England
events.description: Three days after William Rufus died in a hunting accident, his brother Henry was crowned at Westminster. His Charter of Liberties and administrative reforms made him one of England's ablest medieval kings.

events.title: William Wallace is handed over to the English at Robroyston
events.description: Sir John de Menteith, a Scottish knight loyal to Edward I, turned William Wallace over to English soldiers at Robroyston, near Glasgow. Wallace, who had won at Stirling Bridge in 1297, was taken to London and executed for treason.

events.title: Sir Humphrey Gilbert claims Newfoundland for England
events.description: At St John's harbour, Humphrey Gilbert claimed Newfoundland for Elizabeth I, an early step in English overseas expansion. No settlement followed, and Gilbert was lost at sea on the voyage home.

events.title: The first transatlantic telegraph cable is completed
events.description: Cable ships landed the ends of the first telegraph line across the Atlantic in Ireland and Newfoundland. It carried messages for just three weeks before failing, but proved the idea possible.
events.html: Cable ships landed the ends of the first telegraph line across the Atlantic in Ireland and Newfoundland. It carried messages for just three weeks before failing, but proved the idea possible.

events.title: Cornerstone laid for the Statue of Liberty's pedestal
events.description: The cornerstone of the pedestal was laid on Bedloe's Island in New York Harbor. Americans had to raise the funds for the base, while France paid for the statue itself.

events.title: An electric traffic signal is installed in Cleveland
events.description: An electric traffic signal with red and green lights was installed at Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street in Cleveland, Ohio. It is often cited as the first of its kind in the world.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe is found dead in Los Angeles
events.description: Marilyn Monroe was found dead at her home in Brentwood, aged 36; the coroner ruled probable suicide from barbiturates. Her death cut short the career of Hollywood's most famous star.
